answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the jetty ordering is published with the umber batch, the delta audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 45% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 249 account operation therefore ties up 39 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
